title: Backyard Bugs for Kids! 5 Bug Surprises with Pip
intro: Hi, explorers! I'm Pip, and welcome to WildKids Discovery!
Today we're going on a backyard bug hunt to meet five tiny friends.
Can you count them with me? One, two, three, four, five!
Grab your magnifying glass. Let's explore!

lines: Here's our first friend. Here's a clue: it's red with black spots! Can you guess?
Ladybugs have spots on their shiny wing covers.
Different kinds of ladybugs have different numbers of spots.
Can you count the spots with me? One, two, three, four, five, six!
Can you guess why ladybugs are so bright?
Their bright colors tell birds: I taste yucky, don't eat me!
Ladybugs help gardens by protecting the plants.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it buzzes and makes honey! Can you guess?
Honeybees make honey from the sweet nectar in flowers.
Their wings flap super fast. That's what makes the buzz!
Can you buzz like a bee? Bzzzz!
Can you guess how many eyes a bee has?
Five! Two big eyes, and three tiny eyes on top of its head.
Bees do a waggle dance to show friends where the flowers are.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it has big, colorful wings! Can you guess?
Butterflies drink sweet nectar with a long tongue, like a curly straw.
Every butterfly starts out as a little caterpillar.
Can you flutter your arms like butterfly wings?
Can you guess what a butterfly tastes with?
Its feet! Butterflies have tiny tasters on their feet.
Who's next? Here's a clue: it's tiny, but super strong! Can you guess?
Ants live together in big groups called colonies.
Ants talk with smells, and by touching their antennae.
Can you wiggle your fingers like ant antennae?
Can you guess? Can an ant carry something heavier than itself?
Yes! Ants can carry things much heavier than their own bodies.
Ants work together as a team.
Who's last? Here's a clue: it carries its house on its back! Can you guess?
A snail's shell is its home. It goes everywhere with it!
Snails slide along on a slippery trail of slime.
Can you move slowly, slowly, like a snail?
Can you guess where a snail's eyes are?
At the tips of its long tentacles! Way up high.
When it's very dry, a snail can hide in its shell and rest for a long time.

recap: What a bug hunt! Let's remember.
Bright ladybugs tell birds they taste yucky.
And snails have eyes on their tentacles!
outro: Which bug was your favorite? Look closely next time you're outside, and be gentle with every bug.
